Question: For each \(x\) in \([0, 1],\) define \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x, & 0 \le x \le \tfrac{1}{2},\\ 2 - 2x, & \tfrac{1}{2} \lt x \le 1. \end{cases} \] Let \(f^{[2]}(x) = f(f(x)),\) and \(f^{[n+1]}(x) = f^{[n]}(f(x))\) for each integer \(n \ge 2.\) For how many values of \(x\) in \([0, 1]\) is \(f^{[2005]}(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}?\)
Solution:
Method 1: Work backward through the function

Instead of expanding a composition with 2005 copies of \(f\), find all inputs that lead to a given output in one step.

For any \(y\in(0,1)\), the first branch gives \(2x=y\), while the second gives \(2-2x=y\). Thus the two inputs are
\[
x=\frac y2\qquad\text{and}\qquad x=1-\frac y2.
\]
The first lies in \((0,\tfrac12)\), and the second lies in \((\tfrac12,1)\). Both satisfy their branch conditions, are distinct, and remain inside \((0,1)\).

Begin with the single target \(\tfrac12\). After one backward step we have exactly the solutions of \(f(x)=\tfrac12\); after two steps we have exactly the solutions of \(f^{[2]}(x)=\tfrac12\), and so on. Every current target has two preimages. Moreover, different targets cannot share a preimage, because a function assigns only one output to each input. Therefore every step doubles the number of solutions without omission or duplication.

If \(N_n\) is the number after \(n\) backward steps, then
\[
N_0=1,\qquad N_{n+1}=2N_n,
\]
so \(N_n=2^n\). The endpoints introduce no additional solutions: both \(0\) and \(1\) map to \(0\), which stays at \(0\). Hence the requested number is \(\boxed{2^{2005}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

Method 2: Count the straight pieces of each iterate

Each straight piece of an iterate that runs between heights \(0\) and \(1\) contributes exactly one solution at height \(\tfrac12\). We can count these pieces as the function is composed repeatedly.

The graph of \(f\) starts with two straight pieces, joining the points \((0,0)\), \((\tfrac12,1)\), and \((1,0)\). Each piece rises from \(0\) to \(1\) or falls from \(1\) to \(0\).

Because all the compositions use the same function, we may obtain \(f^{[n+1]}\) by applying \(f\) to the values of \(f^{[n]}\). Consider one straight piece of \(f^{[n]}\) running between heights \(0\) and \(1\). At its midpoint the height is \(\tfrac12\). Applying \(f\) sends the two endpoint heights to \(0\), since \(f(0)=f(1)=0\), and sends the midpoint height to \(1\). On either half, the composition is linear. Thus this one piece becomes two straight pieces, each again running between heights \(0\) and \(1\).

Starting with two pieces, the number therefore doubles at every composition. Consequently \(f^{[n]}\) has \(2^n\) such pieces covering \([0,1]\). Each contains exactly one point at height \(\tfrac12\), strictly inside the piece. Adjacent pieces meet only at heights \(0\) or \(1\), so no solution is counted twice.

Taking \(n=2005\) gives \(\boxed{2^{2005}}\) solutions, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
